item.title: A Deep Dive into Kubernetes Network Packet Forwarding
item.description: This article is translated from https://learnk8s.io/kubernetes-network-packets, not word for word, with some of my own understanding worked in. By reading this article, you can learn how packets are forwarded inside and outside Kubernetes, starting from the original web request all the way to the container hosting the application. item.title: How to Make a Port Accessible Only to a Specified IP
item.description: 1. Host Service Ports 1 2 iptables -I INPUT -p tcp --dport 80 -j DROP iptables -I INPUT -p tcp -s 1.2.3.4 --dport 80 -j ACCEPT This allows only 1.2.3.4 to access port 80 on the local host. 2. Docker Service Ports For services started like docker run -d -p 80:80 shaowenchen/demo:whoami, the method above does not work; the rule has to be added to the DOCKER-USER chain.
